title: Layer 2 & Layer 3 Host Verification: ARP Resolution & VirtualBox OUI Analysis
summary: Following subnet migration to 192.168.0.0/24, conducted definitive Layer 2 and Layer 3 host discovery from Kali Linux targeting Metasploitable 2 (192.168.0.155). Verified bidirectional packet routing via ICMP Echo (0% packet loss) and confirmed Layer 2 hardware adjacency through ARP cache inspection, validating the Oracle VirtualBox hardware prefix (08:00:27).

blocks.text: Tested end-to-end IP reachability across the bridged wireless network:

blocks.label: kali
blocks.text:
┌──(general㉿lee)-[~]
└─$ ping -c 2 192.168.0.155
PING 192.168.0.155 (192.168.0.155) 56(84) bytes of data.
64 bytes from 192.168.0.155: icmp_seq=1 ttl=64 time=185 ms
64 bytes from 192.168.0.155: icmp_seq=2 ttl=64 time=3.09 ms

--- 192.168.0.155 ping statistics ---
2 packets transmitted, 2 received, 0% packet loss, time 1014ms
rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 3.086/93.801/184.517/90.715 ms
The return TTL of **64** is the textbook signature of a Linux kernel hop. The second packet RTT dropped to **3.09 ms**, reflecting immediate local Wi-Fi transmission after initial ARP resolution.
Inspected the Linux kernel's ARP table to verify the hardware link without relying on higher-layer network stacks:

blocks.label: kali
blocks.text:
┌──(general㉿lee)-[~]
└─$ arp -n 192.168.0.155
Address                  HWtype  HWaddress           Flags Mask            Iface
192.168.0.155            ether   08:00:27:1d:80:01   C                     eth0

head: Field
Observed Value
Technical Meaning
rows: **Oracle VirtualBox Virtual NIC**. The initial 3 bytes (`08:00:27`) represent the IEEE Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI) allocated to VirtualBox.
The ARP request broadcast was successfully replied to by the target's NIC, and the mapping is cached in memory.
Direct Layer 2 broadcast domain adjacency (both VMs share the bridged wireless adapter).

blocks.text: Earlier when running `arp -n 192.168.0.155` from inside Metasploitable itself, the kernel reported `no entry` because an operating system never issues an ARP request for its own IP. Testing from Kali immediately populated the complete hardware mapping, proving full cross-host communication.
